column1: # The graph is looked for beside the repository's .git, not in the current
# directory: a worktree has no graphify-out/ of its own, and a check keyed on
# the current directory read due in every worktree session whatever the graph's
# age. Sixteen of seventeen recorded session roots here are worktrees.
# Keyed on the checkout that holds the graph, and not on the tree the caller
# happens to be standing in. Those are the same thing in a plain checkout and
# different in a worktree, and the difference made this row a permanent DUE:
# any commit in a worktree is a commit the graph has not seen, sessions commit
# constantly, and sixteen of the seventeen session roots recorded for this
# project are worktrees. Measured at the top of one session: `due` from the
# worktree and `ok` from the checkout beside it, same graph, same second.
# This reverses the reading written here before it — that the commit compared
# against is the one the worktree stands on — and the argument is that the
# refresh that reading asks for cannot do what the DUE says is missing.
# graphify builds the graph from the checkout that holds it, so a refresh run
# while standing in a worktree models the HOLDING checkout's tree and not the
# worktree's unmerged work. It clears the row by moving a file's mtime, which
# is a change of status and not of what the graph models. A row that is on in
# almost every session, and whose remedy does not address the thing it names,
# is the status table this repository already keeps a lesson about.
graphify
column4: refresh the knowledge graph after a merge
column5: G="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)")"; test -n "$(find "$G/graphify-out/graph.json" -newermt "$(git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z "$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)" -- . ":(exclude)projects/*/maintenance.log")" 2>/dev/null)"
